title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen quirks + GQA/MQA tuning
author: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: This PR introduces model-specific runtime optimizations for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen families, focused on kernel selection heuristics, scheduling adjustments, KV cache layout fixes, and quantization tuning for GQA/MQA-backed checkpoints. Motivation: Several customer workloads (long-context chat, multiprompt batching) exposed suboptimal kernel paths and inefficient KV cache handling for recent model variants, especially Qwen-GQA and Mistral's fused-attention layouts. The changes reduce latency variability (p95) and improve throughput for commonly seen seq-len distributions without affecting model accuracy. Changes and checklist: - Kernel selection heuristic: prefer fused MHA / grouped GEMM kernels for Mistral when hidden_dim % group_size == 0. - Rotary/ALiBi fallback fixes: ensure Llama rotary offsets are computed in 32-bit for long-contexts to avoid jitter in kv-cache indexing. - KV cache layout: shard-aware cache layout to reduce cross-GPU memory copies for Dedicated. - GQA/MQA tuning: quantized matmul tiling tweaks and dequant alignment to reduce accumulation error and enable more aggressive MQA profiles. - Scheduler: continuous-batching policy update to favor latency-SLO requests for pinned models (configurable). - Tests: new unit tests for kv-cache indexing, integration perf tests for 1K/4K context windows, and convergence checks for quantized outputs. Checklist: [x] unit tests added, [x] perf harness added, [x] compatibility smoke tests, [x] docs note for model onboarding, [x] canary rollout plan in comments. Commits (summary): - Adapt kernel-selector to prefer fused/multi-head kernels for Mistral (perf/regression safe) - Fix Llama rotary index overflow for long contexts - Implement shard-aware KV cache layout and unit tests - Add GQA/MQA quantization alignment and test vectors - Tune continuous-batcher thresholds and add config flags - Add perf jobs and dashboards updates Testing notes: Initial CI run surfaced a flakiness in the Mistral shader path (GPU kernel mismatch on older drivers). Added a driver-compat guard and fallback to generic GEMM. Local perf runs (A100 and 4090 dev node) show consistent improvements; full cluster canary run on Dedicated passed acceptance gating. Rollout plan: canary on dedicated pool small percent -> monitor p50/p95 and token cost -> release to main pool with automated rollback on error budget exceed. Related: ENG-4821 (model onboarding fragility), ENG-5243 (continuous batching tuning).

review_comments: Samir Patel: Great direction. Two/questions: (1) how does the kernel selector behave for hybrid models (some layers MHA, some not)? (2) Can you add a regression test that runs a few prompt seeds comparing fp32 vs quantized outputs?
Aisha Khan: Answered: kernel selector falls back to per-layer inspection; added a regression test in tests/integration/test_quant_regress.py. Added note in PR description.
Evelyn Wu: The kv-cache copy reduction looks promising. Please add a comment explaining the shard layout and add a small ascii diagram for future readers.
Aisha Khan: Added inline doc + ascii diagram in kv_cache_layout.cpp (see commit c3d4e5f).
Jonah Reed: CI failed on initial run due to driver mismatch on older CUDA 11.8 nodes. We should guard the fused kernel path behind a driver-compat check.
Aisha Khan: Added compat guard (third_party/drivers/compat_guard.cpp) and a fallback to generic gemm; re-ran CI, all checks passed.
ci_checks: perf-canary: pass (canary on dedicated pool, 3% of capacity)
benchmarks: Llama (base) p50: -8% latency, p95: -12%, throughput +9% on 4090 for typical chat load (seq=2048)
Mistral (fused MHA path) p50: -15% latency, p95: -18%, throughput +22% on A100 for seq=1024
Qwen-GQA (MQA tuned) p50: -6% latency, p95: -10%, token cost -4% with negligible output delta (MSE < 1e-4 vs fp32)
End-to-end continuous-batcher change reduced tail latency on mixed workloads by ~10% while increasing aggregated throughput by ~6%
release_notes: Model-specific runtime improvements for Llama, Mistral, and Qwen (GQA/MQA) with better kernel selection and kv-cache layout
Reduced p95 latency and improved throughput for common seq-len distributions
Added configurable flags for continuous batching to favor latency-SLO traffic
Canary rollout will be used; no breaking changes expected
notes: Operational: monitor token-cost dashboards and p95_latency for first 72h after full rollout
If driver-compat guard triggers often, we will add automatic auto-update suggestion for affected nodes
Follow-up: add Qwen-specific microbenchmarks to automated perf suite (ENG-5243)
